references.text: The psalmist's prophetic words about the Messiah's suffering: "they have pierced my hands and my feet" – Jesus shows the disciples exactly these wounds as proof of his identity ([ref:Ps 22:17|Psalms 22:17]).
The prophecy in [ref:Zech 12:10|Zechariah 12:10] that they will look on him whom they have pierced points forward to Jesus' resurrection body bearing nail marks in his hands and feet.
Isaiah's prophecy about the suffering servant who was pierced for our transgressions ([ref:Isa 53:5|Isaiah 53:5]), which finds its fulfillment in the wounds of Jesus that he shows to the disciples.
In [ref:John 20:20|John 20:20], Jesus shows the disciples his hands and his side, parallel to Luke's account, as proof that it is truly him who has risen.
Jesus encourages Thomas to put his finger into the nail holes and his hand into his side ([ref:John 20:27|John 20:27]) – a close parallel to the invitation in Luke to touch him and see.

John's testimony that what they have "touched with their hands" concerning the Word of life ([ref:1 John 1:1|1 John 1:1]), reflects the concrete physical experience the disciples had with the risen Jesus.
Peter testifies in [ref:Acts 10:40-41|Acts 10:40-41] that they ate and drank with Jesus after his resurrection, confirming Jesus' physical, bodily resurrection.

The immediate context in [ref:Luke 24:36-37|Luke 24:36-37] where Jesus suddenly stands among the disciples and they are frightened and think they see a spirit – something Jesus counters by showing them his hands and feet.
Right after this, Jesus eats broiled fish in front of them ([ref:Luke 24:42-43|Luke 24:42-43]), further proof that he has a real physical body and is not a spirit.
Paul writes in [ref:Phil 3:21|Philippians 3:21] about how Christ will transform our lowly body to be like his glorious body – Jesus' resurrection body was truly physical, yet glorified.
